title: Being ambitious and being a dad
titleZh: 雄心勃勃并成为一名父亲
author: nichochar
relevanceReason: 命中 2 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: Being ambitious and being a dad When I was going through YC, I didn’t mention my seven month old daughter to anyone. Now a few years later I have two kids, a dog and a very packed schedule. My kids are the best thing in my life. For years, my work was my life. Now my life competes with my work. I don’t think I’m alone. Here’s Paul Graham in Having Kids:

Some of my worries about having kids were right, though. They definitely make you less productive. I know having kids makes some people get their act together, but if your act was already together, you’re going to have less time to do it in.

I love building, learning, and competing. Life before kids was straightforward: I worked hard and centered my life around things I love: computers, technology, friends. I moved to SF, worked at some awesome companies, met a wonderful girl and built a strong relationship. A huge amount of my time was spent on work, and yet there was still some left for that and more. Turns out, you have a lot of time when you don’t have dependents. All the people I admire most are builders. I have devoured biographies and studied many great founders. Unfortunately this led me to an uncomfortable conclusion: most of them are horrible parents. Steve Jobs literally abandoned his daughter Lisa because “the time wasn’t right” (he was focused on Apple). Einstein abandoned one kid1 and was constantly absent, daydreaming about work around his other two, to the point where his wife divorced him and took them. Elon Musk has so many children and companies that he mechanically cannot spend any significant amount of time with any of them. Edison, Ford, Ferrari,… the list goes on and on. Most biographies of great founders I’ve read have had another story etched in between the lines: a pretty bleak one of a bad parent. I know many ambitious parents; it’s not an uncommon combination. Most of them are willing to make a choice that I will not: delegate the parenting away. I do not believe the quality time theory. I firmly believe in maximizing the quantity of time spent with them; there are no diminishing returns for them on that front. This is somewhat problematic, and unfortunately it gets worse. The time spent is even more important when they’re young, which of course happens to coincide with the prime of my career. I’ll find myself planning my work or reflecting on how much I accomplished today or in the last week and the result is clear. I’m a productive and well organized person, but comparing the output of parent-me to the kidless-me in a given week reveals a visible gap. Everyone knows life is short. Now that I have kids, it feels 10x shorter. This sucks. I am ambitious: I wake up every morning with a burning fire in my stomach to build awesome things. In this, I differ from Paul Graham:
I hate to say this, because being ambitious has always been a part of my identity, but having kids may make one less ambitious.

I am not less ambitious. But I am also ambitious about being a great dad. My anecdotal observations show a pretty strict dichotomy: great fathers and great achievers rarely overlap. Rarely is not never though. Some figures in technology (Paul Graham, DHH, Jeff Dean, even Mark Zuckerberg) seem to be pushing on both fronts with rare success. Often the pattern is early success, but not always. Frankly even if I couldn’t find the pattern, I would still not accept defeat. I don’t have a perfect magical solution. I’m voicing a frustration, but I am also rejecting the choice. I’ve come to redefine ambition for myself: ambition is being a great dad as well as building great things. I acknowledge and accept that it is much more difficult than just aiming for one or the other, and both are hard enough in their own right. But hard is the point of ambition, right? My strategy is pretty simple: stay focused, don’t waste time on bullshit, keep improving execution. I do this by carefully clarifying what I want my work to be, focusing on health to maximize energy, setting clear rules on time with kids (weekday dinners, weekends prioritize family) and completely removing time-wasting activities. With clear goals and discipline, my plan is to achieve compounding gains. I am writing this because I never hear anyone say it. Be ambitious enough to be an ambitious dad. Footnotes

comments.author: spicyusername
comments.textRawHtml:
The older I get the more I realize ambition and "being ambitious" is a completely misplaced way to orient your life.

The chance of validation from others is not a good reason for making one choice or another and a life made of choices of that kind will eventually leave you spiritually bankrupt.

Make decisions based on what you're passionate about, based on what will bring and keep meaningful relationships into your life, based on what will leave you with habits that take you outside, into the sun, moving your body and eating healthy, and, sure, that will afford you the ability to pay for those things.

Focus on the process, not the outcome.

Making decisions based on what will make you more "successful" will make you a slave to others approval. And those others will use you up and waste your life to achieve their own objectives.

Also, if you pick the right partner, having kids does all the good things in life at once. It is the most efficient way to get yourself into the good life possible.
comments.textZhHtml:
年龄越大，我越意识到雄心勃勃，而“雄心勃勃”是一种完全错误的人生方向。

他人认可的机会并不是做出这样或那样的选择的好理由，由这种选择组成的生活最终会让你在精神上破产。

根据你所热衷的事情、基于什么会给你的生活带来并保持有意义的关系、基于什么会让你养成习惯来做出决定。你在户外，沐浴在阳光下，活动身体，健康饮食，当然，这会让你有能力支付这些费用。

关注过程，而不是结果。

根据什么能让你更“成功”做出决定，会让你成为别人认可的奴隶。而那些人会耗尽你的精力，浪费你的生命来实现他们自己的目标。

此外，如果你选择了正确的伴侣，生孩子会同时带来生活中所有美好的事情。这是让自己进入美好生活的最有效方式。

children.author: vadoff
children.textRawHtml:
Being ambitious doesn't necessarily mean you're aiming for validation. It means you're aiming for a goal that's challenging. What drives that ambition is what matters.

Many are driven by a desire to create real change, a desire to build, to solve a problem, and/or help people. Many do it simply because it's fun, but it doesn't make them any less ambitious.
children.textZhHtml:
雄心勃勃并不一定意味着您的目标是获得验证。这意味着您正在瞄准一个具有挑战性的目标。驱动这一雄心壮志的因素才是最重要的。

许多人的驱动力是创造真正的改变、建设、解决问题和/或帮助人们的愿望。许多人这样做只是因为它很有趣，但这并没有降低他们的雄心。

children.author: amouat
children.textRawHtml:
I don't disagree, except that you've taken ambitious to mean climbing the corporate ladder, which is a relatively narrow reading.

It can also mean wanting a achieve a large dream or goal e.g. writing a book.
children.textZhHtml:
我并不反对，只是你认为雄心勃勃意味着攀登公司阶梯，这是一个相对狭窄的解读。

它也可能意味着想要实现一个伟大的梦想或目标，例如写一本书。

children.author: tyre
children.textRawHtml:
I can +1 who you're replying to in the context of founders and achieving a large dream (building a massive company.)

I was in the Summer 2016 batch. Ten years out feels like long enough for some reflections on lives well-lived. There were people in my batch who were ambitious, not in climbing someone else's corporate ladder but in building their own massive/successful/wealthy company.

For those who separated it from what they were passionate about—and here I mean the impact, not "passionate about building a big business—there have been more than a few crash outs. Existential crises, Extremely Online Syndrome, pulled into a world where what VCs say or competition with press releases on Tech Crunch define their self-worth.

These people are generally not happy. Some are! But many are not.

The founders who worked on things that they care about, with technology or company-building as a _means_ to achieving some greater end, are doing much better. They might or might not still be at their start-ups. Many have gone on to work at other impactful companies or organizations. They seem much more content with life and their contributions to the world.

That's the type of ambition that is healthy _and_ meaningful _and_ lasting. It's not that these people aren't ambitious—they very much are! But it's not "big company good". It's "big positive impact good."
children.textZhHtml:
我可以在创始人和实现远大梦想（建立一家大型公司）的背景下为您回复的人 +1。

我参加了 2016 年夏季批次。十年后的时光似乎足够长，足以让我们反思美好的生活。我这批人中有些人雄心勃勃，不是为了攀登别人的公司阶梯，而是为了建立自己的庞大/成功/富裕的公司。

对于那些将其与他们所热衷的事情分开的人来说，这里我指的是影响，而不是“热衷于建立一个大企业，已经发生过多次崩溃。存在危机，极端在线综合症，把他们带入了一个风投们所说的或与 Tech Crunch 上的新闻稿竞争的世界。定义他们的自我价值。

这些人通常不快乐！但很多人并不快乐。

那些以技术或公司建设作为实现更大目标的创始人，他们可能会或可能不会继续在其他有影响力的公司或组织工作。他们似乎对生活和对公司的贡献更加满意。

这种野心是健康的、有意义的、持久的。这并不是说这些人没有野心——他们非常有野心！但这不是“大公司的好事”，而是“有巨大的积极影响的好事”。

children.author: Aurornis
children.textRawHtml:
Or the dream of financial security and early retirement, which are both highly valuable in the context of having a family.

I couldn’t care less about the external validation part of it or my job title.
children.textZhHtml:
或者是财务安全和提前退休的梦想，这对于拥有一个家庭来说都是非常有价值的。

我不在乎它的外部验证部分或我的职位。

children.author: glitchc
children.textRawHtml: I think the OP's logic applies. Every author is hoping their book is a best-seller and/or wins awards i.e. the approval of others.
children.textZhHtml: 我认为OP的逻辑适用。每个作者都希望自己的书成为畅销书和/或获奖，即得到他人的认可。

children.author: sokoloff
children.textRawHtml:
I know a couple of O’Reilly authors. I don’t think any of them expected a best-seller or awards from their work, just “I get a high-four or barely-five figure payment for a competent treatment of a technical topic.”

Maybe you could argue that’s a lightweight version of “approval of others”
children.textZhHtml:
我认识几位 O’Reilly 作者。我认为他们中的任何一个人都没有期望自己的作品能成为畅销书或奖项，只是“我因为对某个技术主题的出色处理而获得了四位数或不到五位数的报酬。”

也许你可能会说这是“他人认可”的轻量级版本

children.author: theF00l
children.textRawHtml:
Surprised to hear that an O'Reilly book will net you less than a month of work for a SWE in the US and some parts of Europe.

But I guess the reward is not the money but the expertise and signal.
children.textZhHtml:
很惊讶地听说，一本 O'Reilly 的书可以让你在美国和欧洲部分地区为 SWE 工作不到一个月的时间。

但我想回报不是金钱，而是专业知识和信号。

children.author: spicyusername
children.textRawHtml:
Focusing on your passion for writing is more likely to produce the book than focusing on your desire to be able to say you were someone who finished a book.

And who is being able to say you were someone who finished a book for? You? Or is it for someone else?
children.textZhHtml:
专注于你对写作的热情比专注于你想要说你是读完一本书的人更有可能写出这本书。

谁能说你是读完一本书的人呢？你？还是给别人的？

children.author: code51
children.textRawHtml: Or the dream of keeping a stable job.
children.textZhHtml: 或者保持稳定工作的梦想。

children.author: afavour
children.textRawHtml: While I agree with everything you say... I'd sure like to earn more money. It would make my life better and my kid's lives better. The surest path to achieving that is to be ambitious in the workplace. It's something I find myself constantly conflicted on.
children.textZhHtml: 虽然我同意你所说的一切......我确实想赚更多的钱。这会让我的生活变得更好，也让我孩子的生活变得更好。实现这一目标的最可靠途径是在工作场所雄心勃勃。这是我发现自己经常感到矛盾的事情。

Do the things for the things in themselves.

为事物本身而做事。

children.author: faeyanpiraat
children.textRawHtml: I kinda agree with you but Could you please elaborate on “ having kids does all the good things in life at once” as I dont see how is that so straightforward. I’m actually currently really conflicted on the idea whether I want or dont want kids.
children.textZhHtml: 我有点同意你的观点，但你能否详细说明一下“生孩子可以同时做生活中所有美好的事情”，因为我不明白这怎么这么简单。其实我现在很矛盾，不知道要不要孩子。

children.author: Aurornis
children.textRawHtml:
Looking back, I found most Internet comment section advice about having kids to be unhelpful. There’s a cliche that gets rephrased 1000 different ways to say a variation of “It’s a lot of work and my kids drive me crazy but I wouldn’t trade it for the world”. Now that I am a parent that advice feels like it oversells the negatives and fails to explain why people like their kids.

Truthfully, it is hard to relate to non-parents why you enjoy your own kids. It’s completely different than babysitting someone else’s kids. It’s your family and you like being with them. After work I’d rather hang out with my kids and go for a bike ride or build legos with them instead of relax and watch TV. I’m kind of dreading the day that they don’t want to spend so much time with me because we have so much fun. It’s a little extra motivation to get my work done early and start my day early so I can have more time with them, which is something I never thought I’d say as a nights and evenings person.

The extra work is more work than if I didn’t have kids and just relaxed after work and on weekends, but it’s not the world-ending grind like some people talk about. The early part where they’re waking up through the night and need constant feedings and changes goes by quickly and then you’re into a routine and teaching them ever more self sufficiency. I wouldn’t dwell on it, or at least don’t let it be an obstacle to imagining the rest of your years with a family. It’s a year or two of altered sleep schedules for 40 years of having a family.

Getting balanced takes from happy parents around you is a good idea. Online it’s too easy to get drawn into social media whirlpools of unhappy parents venting about things, but I’ve found the best advice comes from the happy parents around you that are quietly enjoying their lives without bringing up the topic of kids. You have to bring it up with them. Depending on where you work, it’s possible that the average person around you has a family and is happy about it, but they’re not bringing it up all the time because it’s just normal life for them.
children.textZhHtml:
回想起来，我发现大多数互联网评论部分关于生孩子的建议都是无益的。有一句陈词滥调可以用 1000 种不同的方式来表达：“工作量很大，我的孩子让我发疯，但我不会用它来换取整个世界”。现在我是一名家长，这些建议感觉过分夸大了负面因素，并且无法解释为什么人们喜欢他们的孩子。

说实话，很难与非父母理解为什么你喜欢自己的孩子。这与照顾别人的孩子完全不同。这是你的家人，你喜欢和他们在一起。下班后，我宁愿和孩子们一起出去骑自行车或和他们一起拼搭乐高积木，而不是放松地看电视。我有点害怕有一天他们不想花那么多时间和我在一起，因为我们玩得很开心。早点完成工作并早点开始新的一天是一种额外的动力，这样我就可以有更多的时间和他们在一起，这是我作为一个夜以继日的人从来没有想过会说的话。

额外的工作比我没有孩子、下班后和周末放松要多，但这并不像一些人谈论的那样是世界末日的苦差事。他们在夜间醒来并需要不断的喂养和变化的早期阶段很快就过去了，然后你就进入了日常生活并教他们更加自给自足。我不会详述它，或者至少不会让它成为你想象与家人共度余生的障碍。拥有一个家庭 40 年，需要一两年改变睡眠时间表。

从周围快乐的父母那里获得平衡的看法是个好主意。在网上，很容易陷入社交媒体的漩涡，因为父母会发泄不满，但我发现最好的建议来自于你周围快乐的父母，他们安静地享受自己的生活，而不会提起孩子的话题。你必须和他们一起提出来。根据您工作的地点，您周围的普通人可能有一个家庭并且对此感到高兴，但他们不会一直提起这件事，因为这对他们来说只是正常的生活。

children.author: mysterydip
children.textRawHtml: I was on the fence for a long time as well. It just looked like a lot of work. And not to sugar coat it, it _is_ a lot of work. But it’s also been so rewarding. You get to see someone experience things for the first time, like riding a bike or eating a tomato. Teaching them it’s ok to have feelings, helping them overcome their fears, watching them make friends. Giving them the advice I wished I had heard from someone I trusted growing up. And a million other things. And the hug and kiss at night with “I love you daddy” can’t be replicated.
children.textZhHtml: 我也持观望态度很长一段时间。看起来工作量很大。不要粉饰它，这需要大量的工作。但它也非常有益。你会看到有人第一次经历一些事情，比如骑自行车或吃西红柿。教导他们有感情是可以的，帮助他们克服恐惧，看着他们交朋友。向他们提供我希望从我成长过程中信任的人那里听到的建议。还有一百万个其他的东西。而晚上的“我爱你爸爸”的拥抱和亲吻是无法复制的。

children.author: OvervCW
children.textRawHtml:
Surely a lot of this can be experienced by associating with parents and their children rather than having them yourself, right?

This may sound somewhat reductive, and please correct me if that is the case, but I find that I can be around and play with my nephew and experience all of this wonder and how he progresses through life, while not being around for the sleepless nights and tantrums that I feel are the "work" part of being a parent.
children.textZhHtml:
当然，通过与父母和他们的孩子交往，而不是自己拥有他们，可以经历很多这样的事情，对吧？

这可能听起来有点简单，如果是这样的话，请纠正我，但我发现我可以和我的侄子一起玩，体验所有这些奇迹以及他在生活中的进步，而不是在我觉得是作为一个“工作”部分的不眠之夜和发脾气的时候。家长。
